comment: SPEC-016 office dressing: the task's arm on the desk it works at, colourful manipulables around it, and a warm shell. Props are chosen by measurement, not by name: rfw_w.scenes.visualization.pick_colourful_props ranks the library's own diffuse textures by hue variety first and saturation second -- ranking on saturation alone picked a 'Rubik Cube' whose texture is a single abstract orange wash, and it rendered as a plain orange block. Each pick is then prepared through the production SimReady provider and its prepared height compared with the library's own box, because v1.3's up-axis is per-asset and 10 of 24 earlier candidates came out lying on their side. Everything here is figure-only: no gate in the source delivery judged any of it, and the arm's physics and IK are not_run.
shell_materials_note: flat albedo, not a texture: the request carries a surface per role, not an image, so this warms the box without pretending to be a material scan. No `ceiling` role -- the dollhouse shell has its ceiling removed, and declaring it failed the render with SHELL_MATERIAL_OVERRIDE_BOUND_NOTHING(ceiling), which is the gate doing its job.

additions.why: on the shared table, at its west end; the yaw puts the tool point on the bearing to the mug the task names (cup at -63.2 deg from the base, TCP at -10.2 deg in the arm's own frame), 0.493 m away against a measured 0.8027 m reach

support_table.why: one shared 1.20 x 0.70 x 0.75 m work table in every room, so the three rows compare
